blindSummary:
Trans visitors face severe risk here, and the documented pattern is grim: a trans woman was tortured and murdered in the capital in July 2023; a second trans woman's murder in March 2024 was met with a police response lacking comprehensive investigation; several other trans people were physically assaulted, including by police themselves; and two trans women were detained under a catch-all public-order "hooliganism" charge for making noise. State-affiliated media airs targeted discriminatory hate speech. Trans people face total economic marginalisation (black-market work, precarious housing).

Nothing formally criminalises gender expression, but police are perpetrators rather than protectors, and the state is one of the world's more closed authoritarian systems — there is no recourse and no community infrastructure that can operate openly. An April 2024 ruling by a regional human-rights court found violations in the state's treatment of LGBTI applicants.

For a visitor: no statute bars entry or expression, but discovery risks police abuse with no remedy, and the murder-impunity pattern is documented.
blindOutOfScope: Economic exclusion data is resident-facing; police-perpetrator pattern is traveler-relevant.
blindLocalsOnly: The economic marginalisation data (black-market work, precarious housing) is resident-facing; the police-perpetrator pattern is traveler-relevant.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2025 (covering 2024), chapter on this country: documents the March murder of a trans woman in the capital met with an inadequate police investigation; state-affiliated television airing discriminatory hate speech against LGBTI people after an International Women's Day march demanding trans healthcare access; a family forcibly transporting an 18-year-old woman to the capital after she came out; and an April ruling of a regional human-rights court on the September 2017 police arrests and mistreatment of LGBTI people, which the state acknowledged in 2019.

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2024 (covering 2023), chapter on this country: documents a July police raid on a private birthday party where queer guests were subjected to forced medical examinations, physical and sexual harassment, and threats of outing; an LGBTI media-monitoring project found 77% of 428 analysed media pieces hateful or biased against LGBTIQ people; and an activist being told to remove a rainbow flag in a capital-city cafe.

Regional online news feature on trans people in this country: discrimination has direct economic impacts - trans people are rejected from jobs and housing, pushed into black-market work and precarious housing. Profiles a 29-year-old trans woman: arrested, denied housing and employment, dependent on community support after a trans-friendly employer of hers shut down.

International human-rights organisation (Oct 2017): this country's anti-gay crackdown - police raids in the capital in September 2017 detained dozens of LGBT people on bogus charges, with beatings and forced medical examinations documented; the organisation called for investigation and release.

A national LBT rights organisation's shadow report to the UN women's-discrimination treaty body (44th session): documents state-approved ignorance, employment discrimination, militant homophobia/transphobia in official and private media, forced marriages, and the impossibility of changing identity documents for trans women; the organisation serves 200+ LBT people.

Foreign broadsheet (Sept 2017): outcry as police in this country launch a crackdown on the LGBT community - at least 60 people imprisoned or fined after raids in the capital; part of a wave of arrests ahead of a major international multi-sport games the capital hosted that year.

Regional-affairs outlet (May 2012): the country's pop-music scene versus religious conservatism - senior clerics in a neighbouring theocracy demanded that the capital cancel a major international music contest it was about to host and shun any 'gay pride', dismissing both as foreign degendency; a senior presidential official publicly ruled out ever hosting a gay parade - documented pressure on LGBT visibility from abroad.
